cmds: # the OTW Krypton0 page itself gives this Base64 string
# documented technique: /krypton/krypton1/krypton2 is ROT13 — tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m' decodes 'YRIRY GJB CNFFJBEQ EBGGRA' to 'LEVEL TWO PASSWORD ROTTEN'
ssh krypton2@krypton.labs.overthewire.org -p 2231  # verify the published password logs in
# documented technique: /krypton/krypton2/krypton3 is a Caesar cipher — a single fixed shift applied to every letter; shifting back yields the password
ssh krypton3@krypton.labs.overthewire.org -p 2231  # verify the published password logs in
# documented technique: /krypton/krypton3 uses a monoalphabetic substitution cipher — frequency analysis on the longer found1/found2/found3 ciphertexts recovers the substitution alphabet
ssh krypton4@krypton.labs.overthewire.org -p 2231  # verify the published password logs in
# documented technique: Vigenere cipher with a known key length of 6 — per-position frequency analysis recovers the key FREKEY, which decrypts krypton5 ('HCIKV RJOX') to CLEARTEXT
ssh krypton5@krypton.labs.overthewire.org -p 2231  # verify the published password logs in

# documented technique: Vigenere again but the key length is not given — determine it (index of coincidence / frequency analysis over found1-3), recover the key the same way, decrypt the short krypton6 ciphertext
ssh krypton6@krypton.labs.overthewire.org -p 2231  # verify the published password logs in

# documented technique: /krypton/krypton6/encrypt6 implements an LFSR stream cipher — feeding it known plaintext exposes the keystream, and the recovered password decrypts the krypton7 file (the password itself hints: LFSR IS NOT RANDOM)
ssh krypton7@krypton.labs.overthewire.org -p 2231  # verify the published password logs in

out: (login verified — final account; Krypton series complete)

goals.0: The Krypton intro page shows a Base64 string — decode it to get the first password.
goals.1: The password file for the next level sits in /krypton/krypton1, rotated by ROT13.
goals.2: A Caesar cipher — one fixed shift for every letter — hides the password in /krypton/krypton2.
goals.3: A monoalphabetic substitution cipher in /krypton/krypton3 — letter-frequency analysis on the sample texts breaks it.
goals.4: Vigenere with a known key length of 6 — frequency analysis per key position recovers the key.
goals.5: Vigenere again, but the key length is unknown — work it out first, then repeat the frequency attack.
goals.6: encrypt6 is an LFSR stream cipher — known plaintext exposes the keystream, and LFSRs are not random.
goals.7: Final account: logging in as krypton7 completes the Krypton series.
